title: Finite reductions of immersion pullback preserve constructibility and bounds
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbb Q_\ell$ and an immersion $f:Y\to X$ of arbitrary schemes. Let $K$ be a derived module over the completed integral coefficient ring on $X$, $n\ge0$, and $r,s\in\mathbb Z$. If the detailed $(n+1)$st finite reduction of the normalized coefficient transport of $K$ is intrinsically finite-torsion constructible and has cohomological support contained in $[r,s]$, then the same holds for the $(n+1)$st finite reduction of normalized transport of the actual ordinary derived pullback of $K$. No completeness, uniformity in n, Noetherian condition, or nonempty-interval assumption is required.

proof.text: Normalized quotient and completed coefficient identifications intertwine every projection. Their scalar adjunctions identify detailed finite reduction with canonical adic finite reduction. Compose this identification with finiteComparison to express the target as exact finite coefficient inverse image of the source, transported along coefficient equivalences.

Exact coefficient restriction preserves and reflects zero objects and constructible cohomology. Finite coefficient inverse image commutes with cohomology and pulls back a finite locally closed stratification and its finite constant models. Thus each target cohomology sheaf is constructible.

Outside the same interval source cohomology is zero, and exact inverse image preserves zero. Target support is contained in the same finite integer interval, proving both its finite-support condition and its specified bound, also for an empty interval or scheme.
